blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Pretrained 3D encoders are typically developed on globally reconstructed
scenes expressed in a consistent world coordinate frame, whereas embodied
systems must reason from partial, viewpoint-dependent observations in camera
coordinates. We show that this shift from globally learned 3D feature spaces
to realistic partial observations exposes a severe representation mismatch,
which we find consistently across representative state-of-the-art encoders,
including Sonata and Concerto. A frozen Sonata encoder with a global linear
probe achieves 72.47 mIoU on full ScanNet scenes, but only 2.57 mIoU on
single-frame camera-coordinate inputs. Training-free gravity alignment
recovers performance to 41.64 mIoU, showing that coordinate-frame mismatch
is a dominant source of degradation but cannot be fully resolved through
canonicalization alone. We introduce PAGER , a label-free adaptation method that aligns
partial-view features with a frozen global 3D semantic space using only paired
partial/global geometry. It learns lightweight adaptation modules while
keeping the pretrained encoder and global segmentation probe frozen.
Matched-point feature alignment anchors partial features to their global
counterparts, while relational supervision preserves their similarity
structure with respect to the global representation. Global geometry provides
supervision only during training. Inference operates directly on the partial
observation. Without partial-view labels, PAGER outperforms label-supervised PEFT on both Sonata and Concerto, and in zero-shot ScanNet → \rightarrow ScanNet++ transfer surpasses fully fine-tuned Sonata ( 53.93 53.93 vs. 48.09 48.09 mIoU), suggesting that preserving the frozen global representation can improve cross-dataset transfer.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Large-scale 3D representation learning has significantly advanced semantic scene understanding, enabling pretrained point-cloud encoders to transfer effectively to downstream tasks such as semantic/instance segmentation, and scene parsing ( Qi et al., 2017 ; Zhao et al., 2021 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Schult et al., 2023 ; Xie et al., 2020 ; Wu et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024a ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) . Most existing models, however, are developed and evaluated on globally reconstructed scenes, where geometry is aggregated across views in a consistent world-coordinate frame ( Dai et al., 2017 ; Yeshwanth et al., 2023 ) . This setting differs from realistic embodied perception, where an agent observes only a partial point cloud from its current viewpoint, with incomplete geometry, occlusions, limited FOV, and camera-coordinate inputs (Fig. 1 ). Similar viewpoint gaps have been studied in egocentric and ego-exo video representation learning ( Grauman et al., 2022 ; Grauman et al., 2023 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) , but their effect on pretrained 3D point-cloud representations remains underexplored.

blocks.en: We show that this gap is not merely a consequence of missing geometry, but a severe representation mismatch between globally learned 3D feature spaces and view-constrained partial observations. Using Sonata ( Wu et al., 2025 ) as a strong representative pretrained encoder, we find that a frozen encoder with a global linear probe reaches 72.47 72.47 mIoU on full ScanNet scenes, but drops to 2.57 2.57 mIoU on single-frame camera-coordinate partial views. Notably, when the same partial views remain expressed in world coordinates, performance remains much higher at 67.45 67.45 mIoU (Sec. 3 ). This indicates that camera-coordinate partial inputs can lose compatibility with the semantic feature space learned from globally reconstructed scenes. Recent progress in monocular and multi-view 3D reconstruction ( Wang et al., 2024b ; Wang et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2025b ) further motivates this setting, as view-constrained 3D observations are becoming increasingly available from casually captured visual input.
blocks.zh: 我们显示,这一差距不仅仅是缺少几何学的结果,而是全球学识的3D特征空间与观景限制部分观测之间的严重表现不匹配. 使用 Sonata (Wu等人,2025年)作为一个强大的具有代表性的预先训练的编码器,我们发现一个带有全球线性探测器的冷冻编码器在ScanNet全景上达到了72.47 72.47 mIoU,但在单帧相机坐标部分视图上下降到2.57 2.57 mIoU. 值得注意的是,当世界坐标中仍然有同样的部分观点时,67.45°67.45′mIoU(第3节)的绩效仍然高得多。 这表明相机坐标部分输入可能失去与从全球重建场景中吸取的语义特征空间的兼容性. 最近在单视和多视的立体重建方面取得的进展(Wang et al., 2024b;Wang et al., 2025a;Wang et al., 2025b)进一步激发了这种设置,因为视力约束的立体观测越来越能从随机捕获的视觉输入中获取.

blocks.en:
A straightforward solution is to fine-tune the pretrained encoder on labelled camera-view point clouds fully. This means updating the full encoder backbone together with a segmentation head using dense semantic supervision on the target partial-view training split.
While this can be effective in-domain, it is computationally and storage expensive since each target setting requires an independently adapted model. It also depends on dense semantic annotations of partial 3D observations, which are costly to obtain, and may reduce cross-dataset generalization when only limited labelled views are available.
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT)
reduces the number of updated parameters ( Houlsby et al., 2019 ; Hu et al., 2022 ; Li & Liang, 2021 ; Zaken et al., 2022 ) , and
geometry-aware methods such as GEM ( Tang et al., 2025 ) have shown that
lightweight spatial adaptation can be effective for 3D scene segmentation. However, existing PEFT methods rely on semantic supervision in the target domain and have not been applied to partial-view segmentation, where label biases and missing scene context further limit their effectiveness.

blocks.en:
To address this limitation, we propose PAGER , a label-free partial-to-global adaptation framework
that maps partial camera-coordinate observations back into the semantic
feature space of a frozen globally pretrained model. Our key premise is that
adapting individual features independently is insufficient: a partial
observation should recover not only the global feature associated with the
same physical point, but also its relationships to the broader global
representation.

blocks.en:
We therefore derive two complementary forms of supervision entirely from
paired partial/global geometry. First, matched-point feature anchoring aligns
each partial feature with the global feature of the corresponding physical
point. Second, a point-specific relational objective preserves how that
feature relates to reference features sampled from the global scene. This
transfers structure from the complete-scene representation without requiring
semantic annotation of the partial observations. The pretrained encoder and
global segmentation probe remain frozen throughout adaptation. Paired global
geometry is used only during training. At inference, PAGER operates
directly on partial camera-coordinate point clouds and requires neither the
complete scene nor camera pose.

blocks.en:
We evaluate PAGER under a partial-view semantic segmentation protocol constructed from standard 3D scene datasets, including ScanNet and ScanNet++ ( Dai et al., 2017 ; Yeshwanth et al., 2023 ) . On ScanNet, PAGER reaches 65.46 65.46 mIoU, outperforming adapter-based PEFT ( Houlsby et al., 2019 ) and GEM ( Tang et al., 2025 ) without partial-view semantic labels.
In cross-dataset transfer from ScanNet to ScanNet++, PAGER reaches 53.93 53.93 mIoU and surpasses the fully fine-tuned ScanNet Sonata baseline, suggesting that aligning to the frozen global representation can preserve transferability better than adapting the backbone to a labelled source domain.
blocks.zh:

在从ScanNet到ScanNet++的跨数据集传输中,PAGER达到了53.93 mIoU,并超过了完全微调的ScanNet Sonata基线,这表明与冻结的全球代表制保持一致,比将主干线调整为标注的源域更能保持可转移性.

blocks.en: We summarize the contributions as follows:
blocks.zh: 我们总结如下:

blocks.en: • We isolate coordinate-frame mismatch, not missing geometry, as the dominant failure mode of globally pretrained 3D encoders on partial views ( − 67 -67 vs. − 5 -5 mIoU). • We propose PAGER , which repairs this mismatch from paired partial/global geometry alone, keeping the encoder and probe frozen, requiring no global views or camera pose at inference. • With 1.3 1.3 M parameters and no labels, PAGER outperforms supervised PEFT in-domain ( 65.46 65.46 mIoU) and fully fine-tuned Sonata under domain shift ( 53.93 53.93 vs. 48.09 48.09 ).

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 3D representation learning. Point-based and transformer-based architectures have driven rapid progress in 3D semantic segmentation ( Neshev et al., 2025 ; Qi et al., 2017 ; Zhao et al., 2021 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Schult et al., 2023 ) . In parallel, self-supervised pretraining has become the main route to transferable 3D features ( Xiao et al., 2023 ) . PointContrast introduced correspondence-based pretraining on aligned RGB-D observations ( Xie et al., 2020 ) . Masked Scene Contrast and GroupContrast scaled scene-level pretraining and improved semantic grouping ( Wu et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024a ) ; and Sonata explicitly addressed geometric shortcut learning to produce stronger frozen representations ( Wu et al., 2025 ) . However, these models are trained and evaluated primarily on globally reconstructed scenes. Our focus is the deployment gap that arises when such representations are applied to single-view partial observations.

blocks.en:
In contrast, PAGER targets a more challenging deployment setting: adapting
a pretrained global 3D encoder to view-constrained point clouds in
camera coordinates, where both scene context and the coordinate frame differ from
pretraining. Rather than relying on semantic labels, PAGER learns a
lightweight translator from paired partial/global geometry alone. Its
self-distillation objective transfers both local and scene-level structure by
matching similarity relations to shared global keys, addressing the combined
effects of coordinate mismatch and limited context in local views.

blocks.en:
Before introducing PAGER , we quantify the mismatch between globally pretrained 3D encoders
and view-constrained partial observations. The goal is to isolate why the standard
frozen-transfer recipe fails, and what the adaptation module needs to correct.

blocks.en:
Evaluation conditions. We construct four input conditions that progressively increase deployment realism and evaluate them in world and camera coordinate frames (Fig. 2 ). Global is the scene-level point cloud accumulated from all
frames, corresponding to the conventional training and evaluation setting for 3D scene understanding. Room Slice retains one sixth of the global point cloud, obtained by
partitioning the scene into six slices from the room center. It introduces
coarse geometric incompleteness while preserving the world coordinate frame. View Crop is a spatial crop of the global point
cloud centered at a single camera viewpoint, retaining only points within the region a single
frame would observe while keeping full geometric fidelity within
the crop. Single Frame contains the 3D points back-projected from one RGB-D observation, reflecting realistic deployment with limited field of view, missing geometry, and depth noise.

blocks.en: Two separable sources of degradation. Table 1 reveals an asymmetry. Within world coordinates, performance decreases gradually as inputs become more geometrically incomplete: from 72.47 72.47 mIoU on Global down to 67.45 67.45 mIoU on Single Frame, a drop of under 5 points across four conditions spanning the full range from complete to single-frame reconstruction. The pretrained representation is more robust to missing geometry when the coordinate frame is preserved. The coordinate frame tells a completely different story. blocks.en: Why does the coordinate frame matter? The Camera—Global condition applies a single rigid transform to an otherwise unchanged complete scene. The 67-point drop therefore cannot be attributed to missing scene content. The pretrained encoder often relies on world-frame priors (floors below, gravity-aligned axes) that are disrupted under camera coordinates. Standard augmentations could not cover all possible variations introduced by camera frames, leaving this gap unaddressed.

Our goal is to adapt features extracted from partial camera-coordinate observations so that they become compatible with the global feature space learned by f f and the frozen classifier W W , without updating the backbone or requiring semantic labels for the target partial views.

blocks.en: Limitations of Supervised Adaptation. Supervised adaptation is effective in-domain but carries costs: (i) full fine-tuning updates the entire encoder per target setting, requiring dense partial-view labels and risking corruption of the global relational structure learned during pretraining (ii) label-supervised PEFT (e.g., GEM) is parameter-efficient but inherits class taxonomy (iii) pointwise feature regression is label-free but constrains each adapted feature only relative to its own target, leaving inter-feature relationships unconstrained. PAGER requires no semantic labels, treats every point without class assumptions, and constrains inter-feature structure rather than only pointwise targets.

blocks.en: 4.3 Why the two losses are complementary
blocks.zh: 4.3 (中文(简体) ). 为什么这两个损失是相辅相成的

blocks.en: The cosine loss anchors each partial feature to its global target but says nothing about how features relate to each other. The relational loss fills this gap: by matching similarity patterns over shared keys, it constrains inter-feature structure rather than just absolute positions. Tab. 4 (A1) shows the two provide complementary gains.

blocks.en:
Why random keys? An alternative is to sample keys from the anchor’s neighbourhood (e.g., k-NN in world coordinates), but this is counterproductive: spatially adjacent points lie on similar surfaces and produce highly correlated inner products with the anchor. Random sampling avoids this by drawing keys broadly across the scene, while remaining O(M) and trivially parallelizable, in contrast to alternatives such as farthest-point sampling whose cost scales poorly with scene size. Tab. 4 (A2) confirms the predicted drop when k k -NN keys replace random
keys.

blocks.en: In-domain adaptation. On ScanNet, PAGER outperforms label-supervised PEFT on both encoders without partial-view labels (Tab. 2 ), reaching 65.46 65.46 mIoU with Sonata and 71.67 with Concerto versus 59.81 59.81 and 69.90 69.90 for GEM ( Tang et al., 2025 ) . Linear probing and adapter-based PEFT ( Houlsby et al., 2019 ) fail to recover ( 36.17 36.17 – 41.49 41.49 mIoU). The gains are larger in mAcc ( 80.50 80.50 vs. 73.92 73.92 on Sonata, 87.77 87.77 vs. 80.96 80.96 on Concerto), and on Sonata PAGER closes most of the remaining gap to full fine-tuning ( 65.46 65.46 vs. 69.26 69.26 mIoU) with only 1.2 % 1.2\% of the trainable parameters. On the finer-grained taxonomies, PAGER outperforms GEM with Concerto on both ScanNet++ ( 33.97 33.97 vs. 32.86 32.86 ) and ScanNet200 ( 26.73 26.73 vs. 25.06 25.06 ). With Sonata it trails GEM ( 27.38 27.38 vs. 33.27 33.27 and 19.25 19.25 vs. 21.97 21.97 ) but remains above all other supervised PEFT baselines. Qualitative results are shown in Fig. 4 and per-class results in App. A.3 .

blocks.en: Backbone generality. Sonata ( Wu et al., 2025 ) and Concerto ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) differ substantially in pretraining: point-only self-supervision versus joint 2D-3D self-supervision. Yet both collapse on partial camera-coordinate input ( 2.57 2.57 and 4.97 4.97 mIoU, Tab. 2 ), indicating that the representation gap identified in Sec. 3 is a property of global pretraining rather than of a particular encoder. PAGER uses the same adapter and objectives for both and requires only dense per-point features, with no encoder-specific components. That the stronger Concerto representation yields consistent gains over supervised GEM across all three benchmarks suggests PAGER benefits directly from improvements in the underlying pretrained encoder.
blocks.zh: 后骨通论. Sonata(Wu等人,2025年)和Concerto(Zhang等人,2025年)在预训方面差别很大: 点球自超视与联赛2D-3D自超视. 然而,在部分相机坐标输入(2.57 2.57 和 4.97 4.97 mIoU, Tab. 2 )上都崩溃了,表明第3节中确定的代表差距是全球预先训练的财产,而不是特定的编码器。 PAGER对两者使用相同的适配器和目标,只需要密集的每点特性,没有编码器特有的组件. 较强的Concerto代表率在所有三个基准中都比受监督的GEM获得持续收益,这表明PAGER直接受益于基础的预先培训编码器的改进。

blocks.en: Cross-domain evaluation. To assess robustness to distribution shifts, we train PAGER and all baselines exclusively on ScanNet, using only ScanNet partial/global geometry pairs for PAGER ’s self-distillation, and evaluate on ScanNet++ without further adaptation. No ScanNet++ scenes, geometry, or labels are seen during training. We map predictions to the 20 classes used for training. As shown in Tab. 3 , PAGER learns features that are more resilient to domain changes, achieving higher performance when training and testing data come from different distributions. Full fine-tuning is commonly treated as an upper bound, and on ScanNet Partial it is. That bound, however, is local to the source domain: it costs 108.5M updated parameters and dense partial-view labels per setting. Under distribution shift to ScanNet++, this specialisation becomes a liability, the fully fine-tuned model loses 21 mIoU relative to its in-domain score and falls behind PAGER (53.93 vs. 48.09 mIoU), which never modified the backbone.

blocks.en: 5.3 Limitations.

PAGER requires paired partial/global observations during training, which are available for RGB-D datasets with camera poses but not universally. Still, it performs well in zero-shot scenarios. It inherits the frozen probe’s label taxonomy, so new vocabularies require label remapping or a new probe, although the adapted encoder can be reused once new labels are available. And it remains below in-domain Sonata (full + linear) ( 65.46 65.46 vs. 69.26 69.26 mIoU on ScanNet), but closes most of the gap with only 1.2 % 1.2\% of the trainable parameters and outperforms in cross-dataset transfer.
blocks.zh: PAGER要求在培训期间进行配对部分/全球观测,这些观测可用于带相机的RGB-D数据集,但不普遍。 不过,它在零镜头的情景下表现良好。 它继承了冰冻探测器的标签分类学,所以新的词汇需要重新绘制标签或者一个新的探测器,尽管一旦有了新的标签,可以重新使用经过改造的编码器. 而它仍然位于域内索纳塔(完整+线性)(65.46 65.46 vs 69.26 69.26 mIoU on ScanNet)下方,但大部分差距以只有1.2%的可训练参数和超过跨数据集传输的性能拉近.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We presented PAGER , a label-free framework that aligns partial camera-coordinate 3D features with a frozen global semantic space using only paired geometry and no semantic labels. Our analysis isolates coordinate-frame mismatch as the dominant source of degradation in frozen 3D transfer, and show that geometric self-distillation, combining a matched-point cosine anchor with a point-specific relational objective, sufficiently repairs this mismatch without modifying the backbone. PAGER outperforms label-supervised PEFT in-domain and surpasses fully fine-tuned Sonata in zero-shot cross-dataset transfer, using only 1.3M trainable parameters across two distinct pretrained encoders.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了PAGER,一个无标签框架,将部分相机坐标3D特性与只使用对称几何和无语义标签的冰冻全球语义空间相协调。 我们的分析将坐标-帧不匹配作为冷冻的3D转移中退化的主要来源,并显示几何自沉,将匹配点的余弦锚与特定点的关联目标相结合,充分修复了这种不匹配,而不修改主干. PAGER超越了标签监督的PEFT域内,并在零镜头跨数据集传输中超越了完全微调的索纳塔,只使用跨越两个不同预训编码器的1.3M可训练参数.

blocks.en: The same world-space coordinates are also use to construct the voxel-level correspondences used in our loss. For each scene, we perform a nearest-neighbor search in the global space and assign each original partial point cloud coordinate to its closest global scene original coordinate.

blocks.en: To ensure these correspondences remain valid after augmentation, we explicitly track how every point moves throughout the entire transform chain. At the beginning of preprocessing, each point is assigned a persistent origin identifier, and after every point-indexing operation we update the mapping that links the current points back to their original positions. During voxelization, we additionally record which original points correspond to each voxel representative, allowing us to propagate origin-level correspondences into voxel-level correspondences that remain aligned with the subsequent augmentations.

blocks.en: C.4 Broader Impacts
blocks.zh: C.4 更广泛的影响

blocks.en: Reliable partial-view 3D segmentation supports applications such as robotics, AR/VR, and assistive navigation, where embodied agents must reason from limited onboard observations. As with any indoor scene understanding system, deployment in human-centred environments raises privacy and monitoring considerations that warrant care in real-world use.
blocks.zh: 可靠的部分视图3D分割支持机器人、AR/VR和辅助导航等应用,其中包含的物剂必须从有限的机载观测中找到理由。 如同任何室内场景理解系统一样,在以人为中心的环境中的部署提高了隐私和监测方面的考虑,值得在现实世界中加以注意。
